posts.author: IcySnowflake
posts.body:
Hey all,
I've been in the planning stages for my game for about a year now with the idea it would be created in RPG Maker MV. Recently though I've noticed a lot of tutorials and plugins for MZ specifically that's got me thinking. Which one is better?
I would be developing for both PC and Mobile (that's the plan, anyway), and I already own MV from prior projects that'll probably never see the light of day. But I'm wondering if it's worth the investment to buy MZ or just stick to MV?
If someone could give some pros and cons or their own personal experiences between engines that would be pretty helpful in making such a decision (especially considering in AUD it's $100+ for MZ
)
Cheers!

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
There are kind of a metric butt-ton of threads about this you should be able to find and read through.
Pros for MV:
- you already own it
- it has a slightly larger plugin library, slightly more of which is free and unobfuscated (can be edited for your purposes)
Pros for MZ:
- better mapping interface
- some minor upgrades to the editor which are beneficial if you have it but not really a reason to buy it
- support for modern MacOS
- support for Effekseer animations, if you like the look of those
I think most people will say it's not worth spending money on MZ if you already have MV, unless releasing for Mac is important to you. That being said, Black Friday in the states is coming up, so you would be able to take advantage of a significant discount then.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Just google it because we have had a thousand threads on the subject.
In summary:

Choose MZ for modern features, better mapping, QoL.

posts.body: Your gonna see a 50/50 split of which one people recommend.  No one knows which one is best for you cause it depends on your plans.

posts.author: utunnels
posts.body: MZ is more touch screen friendly. If you want to create something that plays on mobile browsers I think it is better than MV. If you can't make something on MV, you can't expect MZ to do miracle for you. To me they are about the same level. But extra resources and options are always nice to have, so I bought both on a sale.

posts.author: LaCipolla
posts.body:
From experience getting into MZ plugins during the last years: The plugin argument might have been important in the beginning, but it has
considerably
weakened over time! I'm sure there are still some cool, exotic MV-only plugins, but by now, you WILL be able to find every even remotely important function for the MZ as well.
If I'm honest, I think it is kind of ridiculous to recommend MV to a new user now UNLESS they are seriously pressed for money. Which can be an argument, especially if you're doing all of that just for fun!
Since you, the op, are used to the MV already, I can absolutely understand staying with what you know. But investing some money and time for a "serious" project is often a good idea, and we ARE talking about the basic engine of your development here.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
A couple of minor factors:
MV can run on computers that don't have good enough specs for MZ (like my current laptop)
MV can run (via Steam) on Linux
If neither of those are important to you, why not download the monthly trials of each to help you decide? If I get a new PC next year and decide to either use Windows or dual-boot it, I would try MZ because some of the enhancements sound very good to me.
Edited to make the last paragraph more understandable.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
The most concise answer I can give is that MZ is best for all new game makers unless:
You want to push the game mechanics beyond what anyone has done before while making use of existing mods and plugins, and IF you are willing to dive deeply into engine and programming mechanics.  This is the case where you should go with MV or buy both and decide yourself.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Basically,
MV: cheaper, a lot more plugins. The plugins are also cheaper (full Yanfly suite is a lot cheaper than VisuStella) This also means you have a lot more options for any given feature (there are usually half a dozen MV plugins vs maybe one or two for a MZ feature).
MZ: better map editor, Effekseer animations, some other editor improvements.
I have a huge file of edits I've made to plugins, including Yanfly Region Restrictions and Buffs and States Core.
The MZ equivalent of those would be VisuStella which I wouldn't be able to edit. I also have plugins like ZE free jump and Mighty Mouse that don't have MZ equivalents.

posts.author: chewystewy
posts.body: If you're aiming for a smoother experience with modern features, MZ is the way to go—especially if you're targeting mobile. However, if you're tight on budget or just need a stable, tried-and-tested platform for PC, MV might still suit you just fine, especially with your prior knowledge of it.
